scenes.heading: One electron, two outcomes
scenes.narration: Two atoms can end up stuck together in two quite different ways, and the whole difference comes down to what happens to a single electron between them.

scenes.heading: Giving it away
scenes.narration: In ionic bonding one atom transfers an electron outright to the other. Both walk away charged, and those opposite charges are what holds sodium chloride together.

scenes.heading: Sharing it instead
scenes.narration: Covalent bonding never transfers anything. Both atoms keep hold of the same shared pair, which is why covalent partners stay as separate molecules rather than a single block.

scenes.heading: What that changes
scenes.narration: The consequences show up when you heat them. Ionic solids need enormous heat to melt and then conduct electricity, while covalent molecules melt easily and usually conduct nothing at all.

scenes.heading: The single difference
scenes.narration: So one mechanism gives an electron away and the other shares it. Everything else, from what they pair with to how they melt, follows from that one choice.

points: Melting and conducting follow from that
